ledger.claim: Beyond the 75.00 upfront quote, the only contested charge is the 6.00 ERP line for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry — and the driver's own trace never passes that gantry. The nearest of the 289 fixes lies 1159.02 m from the gantry's coordinates, far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 lays down, so the gantry is unmatched and the line is a billing-integrity failure. Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not any deviation is established on this trip.

Because fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is a non-null 75.00, POL-RD-11 fixes the rider's remedy to the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus only those pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The quote of 75.00 equals base, distance, time and platform fee exactly, and the sole pass-through line — the unmatched ERP gantry — is not properly chargeable, so the whole 6.00 excess (81.00 less 75.00) is refundable in full under POL-RD-11(a).

The driver's own statement — 'Local roads were faster that day' — is an admission that he did not drive the CTE expressway, which is exactly what the trace shows: its closest approach to the charged gantry is 1159.02 m. His further submission that 'the ERP is part of the fare package' cannot make chargeable a gantry his own vehicle never crossed, and POL-RD-09 settles pass-through lines on what was actually crossed, not on what the booking engine assumed.

To the extent the driver seeks to excuse the route as traffic-driven, POL-RD-03 exonerates only where a traffic_advisory names a road the optimal route traverses. The only advisory artifact in this case, EV-ADVIS-00532-01, is MISSING — I disclose that it carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and has no payload. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, and the absence of that advisory is itself citable.

Nothing in the trace forces escalation. It is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 289 fixes at a 10 s cadence over 100% coverage, zero gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap, with admissibility status COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Nor does POL-RD-10(8) fire, because the only charge line lacking a counterpart in the trace is the ERP line, and that line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. The money can be decided on this record.

I do not press a distance refund, and I say so plainly. The trace-derived excess is 3.49 km, 12.46% of the 28.0 km optimal, which fails the 20% limb of the POL-RD-01 establishment test — both limbs must pass — and, independently, POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip however large the excess. The rider's money on this trip is in the pass-through line, not in the distance.

I likewise do not press the suggestion that a second passenger was collected: vehicle_type on this trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary analysis is not engaged and no artifact on the record identifies a co-rider pickup. The claim stands on the phantom gantry, which needs no such finding.

The distance claim fails at the first gate, and it fails on the rider's own side of the ledger. The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 31.49 km against an optimal route of 28.0 km, an excess of 3.49 km or 12.46%, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km AND 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb passes; the percentage limb does not, and both must pass. No deviation is ESTABLISHED, the derived deviation block itself returns the status 'no deviation', and the outcome on distance and time is NO_ACTION. The point cannot be rescued by citing trip_record.actual_distance_km of 31.5 km, which POL-RD-01 says may not be cited for the threshold test - and even on that rounded figure the excess is 12.5%, still nowhere near 20%.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace or from an independent source. He cannot show it: the only trace in the bundle measures a 12.46% excess, and no independent source in this case asserts a larger one. The burden never shifts to the driver, so no exoneration clause ever has to be reached and the rider's characterisation of the trip is not enough.

Even if a deviation existed, the money route is closed. EV-FARE-00532 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 75.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The only sum that can move is any amount by which charged_total (81.00) exceeds the quote (75.00) plus properly chargeable pass-through lines - which is exactly the single 6.00 ERP line, and nothing else.

The rider cannot escape the threshold by attacking the trace, because the trace is clean. EV-GPS-00532 carries 289 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. There is no gap, no jump and no stretched sampling interval, and therefore no data failure for the rider to convert into an ESCALATE. The rider must live with the numbers the trace produces.

The rider's assertion that the driver collected a second passenger changes no figure. This trip is vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline and its co-rider exclusion have no application here. The chat log for the trip contains 0 messages and the trace carries no rider track, so nothing in the bundle evidences a collection, a waypoint or a delay. And in any event the entire measured excess on the driven route is 3.49 km - so even on the assumption most favourable to the rider, any stop is already contained inside a sub-threshold figure.

The driver does not resist the 6.00 ERP line, and it should be understood for exactly what it is: a standalone pass-through correction, not a deviation finding and not a finding about the driver's route. The derived gantry proximity places the nearest fix 1,159.02 m from the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry, outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies, so that line is refunded in full under POL-RD-09(4) whether or not a deviation exists. It is a government-set pass-through that the driver neither sets nor collects; under POL-RD-09(1) it is not added on top of any POL-RD-02 figure (and POL-RD-02 does not run on this upfront-quoted trip in any event); and it leaves the 75.00 of distance and time charges standing untouched.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern and therefore no uplift and no referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both POL-RD-06 limbs (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips). No pattern is established, so the POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is unavailable and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is not warranted. Those are the only two profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test, and both are cited here for that test alone.

The rider's premise that the platform has already refunded half the fare is contradicted by the record he relies on. EV-FARE-00532 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no artifact in this bundle evidences a refund to this rider or to any other rider. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves that present state standing: the charge stays in place unless the rider proves a ground for refund, and apart from the 6.00 ERP pass-through discussed above he has proved none.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver.

WHAT IS REFUNDED. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00532) shows an upfront quote of SGD 75.00 and a total charged of SGD 81.00. The SGD 6.00 difference is a single ERP line for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry, and that line is refunded in full. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00532) never comes within the 250 m crossing radius of that gantry — its closest of 289 fixes is 1,159.02 m away — so the gantry is unmatched and the charge is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refundable whether or not any deviation is established. The same SGD 6.00 is the amount by which the 81.00 charged exceeds the 75.00 quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 (there are none, because the one ERP line was not crossed), so POL-RD-11(a) yields the identical figure; nothing is counted twice and nothing is added on top. Refund: SGD 6.00 of the SGD 81.00 contested. The driver did not resist this line and the rider's 'no gantry, I watched' is borne out by the trace.

WHY THERE IS NO DISTANCE OR TIME REFUND. On the governing trace the trip covered 31.49 km (EV-GPS-00532) against a booked optimal of 28.0 km (EV-TRIP-00532) — an excess of 3.49 km, or 12.46%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% of optimal and 0.8 km; the absolute limb passes but the percentage limb does not, and both must pass, so no deviation is established. The rounded trip-record figure of 31.5 km may not be cited for that test and would not change the result. Independently, EV-FARE-00532 records an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, and POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking and bars any distance-or-time refund however large the excess. The rider's complaint that a second passenger was collected does not move any figure: this is a RYDE_X trip, not a pooled product, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary analysis is not engaged, and the whole measured excess is below the threshold in any event. The rider's comparison with other riders' refunds is not evidence about this trip; each case is decided on its own record.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's statement that 'local roads were faster that day' carries no weight. No traffic advisory supports it — the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00532-01, is missing, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, a blocking admissibility defect), and its absence is itself citable — and an unsupported general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge the driver's burden (POL-RD-08). Because no deviation was established, no exoneration clause (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05) had to be reached, and none of them can restore a distance charge that was never refundable. The driver's point that 'the ERP is part of the fare package' does not make chargeable a gantry his vehicle never crossed: pass-through lines are settled on what was actually crossed, not on what the booking engine assumed. The driver's admission that he did not take the expressway, and that the other passenger was 'a short hop', is consistent with the trace but does not alter the amount.

ON THE DRIVER'S POL-GEN-03 FRAMING. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than NO_ACTION: the present state does not stand in full, because part of the contested amount — the unmatched ERP line — is supported by the evidence and is returned.

NO ESCALATION. Nothing here forces a human review. The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes (289 fixes at 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, 0.0 s maximum gap) and the pre-pass marks it COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-RD-07's limbs (a)–(c) and POL-RD-10(3) do not fire; the trip identifiers on the trip record, trace and fare ledger all match; no timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the ERP line, which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts because it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4). The driver-profile check is also clean: EV-DPROF-00532 shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 250 completed trips, far below both POL-RD-06 limbs, so there is no repeat pattern, no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

REFERRAL. The unmatched gantry line is recorded as a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) (see referrals). It does not delay or displace the refund.

CONFIDENCE. 0.90. The deciding facts — the unmatched gantry line and the upfront quote — are carried by EV-GPS-00532 and EV-FARE-00532, both at weight 1.0, and the missing advisory carries no deciding fact and so does not cap this ruling; the floor of 0.70 is comfortably cleared.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — the SGD 6.00 ERP line for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry on EV-FARE-00532 was charged although the trip's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00532) never came within the 250 m match radius of that gantry (closest fix 1,159.02 m); the line is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and is referred for billing-integrity review.
